item.title: AI Engineering Loop Becomes Mainstream with Agentic Tools and Structured Workflow
item.description:
AI Engineering Loop Becomes Mainstream with Agentic Tools and Structured Workflow

In 2025‑2026 a set of agentic tools and a disciplined engineering loop displaced the myth of one‑shot prompting for software development.

🔍 Overview

  • Most disappointed AI projects assume software can be built with a single prompt – the “one‑shot prompting” myth.
  • AI engineering is actually iterative, incremental, and planning‑heavy.
  • The industry split: some think AI writes the software, others see AI as a candidate generator that needs a disciplined loop to become production code.

🗓️ Timeline of Key Milestones

  • 2020 – Retrieval‑augmented generation introduced.
  • 2022‑2023 – Tool‑use and reasoning loops (the ReAct pattern) landed.
  • 2023‑2024 – Agents and the “harness” idea followed.
  • Late 2024 – Model Context Protocol published.
  • 2025 – Claude Code moved from preview to general availability.
  • April 2025 – GitHub Copilot agent mode rolled out to stable.
  • October 2025 – Agent Skills and the SKILL.md convention arrived; through 2026 the pattern went mainstream with a skills marketplace, industry plugins, cloud‑hosted managed agents, and multi‑agent workflows.
  • Late 2025 onward – Models follow written guidelines and guardrails reliably, making a governed, file‑based agentic setup production‑viable.

♻️ The AI Engineering Loop

  1. Plan deeply – Write the destination as behavior (≈ 500 words). Include Out of Scope and Assumptions.
  2. Generate fast – The agent builds vertical slices, starting with the riskiest unknown (a tracer bullet through the whole stack).
  3. Verify hard – Read the code; judgment is checked here. Passing tests is not “done”; it unlocks the next loop.
  4. Own the result – Findings become new issues that feed back into generation.
  5. Repeat – Each pass ships a thin, verified slice; the loop is tight, not skipped.

📊 Evidence of Impact

  • The 70 % problem (Addy Osmani): AI reliably nails the first ~70 % of a task – scaffolding, boilerplate, common patterns.
  • The remaining 30 % requires human judgment.
  • Code can be produced at roughly 1,600 lines a day but safely reviewed at about 400 lines an hour – four hours of careful review for every day of output.
  • 84 % of developers now use or plan to use AI tools, yet only about a third trust the output.
  • One‑shot prompting is the fastest way to “rack it up”, but the fix is cultural: replace dump‑and‑review with verify‑then‑merge.

🚀 Tool Availability

  • Claude Code – General availability in 2025.
  • GitHub Copilot agent mode – Stable release in April 2025.
  • Agent Skills & SKILL.md – Introduced Oct 2025; now mainstream through 2026 with a skills marketplace and multi‑agent workflows.
  • Models from late 2025 onward reliably follow written guardrails, enabling production‑grade, file‑based agentic setups.

The shift from a single prompt to a repeatable, verified loop delivers faster generation while preserving safety and quality.

#AIEngineering #AgenticTools #SoftwareDevelopment #AIWorkflow

Source: One-Shot Prompting Is a Myth: The AI Engineering Loop

item.title: ServiceNow Launches AI Workflow Factory for Continuous Agentic Workflow Improvement
item.description:
ServiceNow Launches AI Workflow Factory for Continuous Agentic Workflow Improvement

ServiceNow announced the AI Workflow Factory, a platform that turns workflow improvement into a continuous, agentic AI‑powered loop. The announcement also introduced Flow by ServiceNow, an AI service desk that can be deployed instantly, and highlighted new agent‑to‑agent capabilities emerging from collaborations with Work4Flow and LogicMonitor.

🔍 Overview

  • AI Workflow Factory launches to enable a continuous loop of workflow improvement powered by AI agents.
  • Flow by ServiceNow is a new AI service desk that deploys instantly.
  • Work4Flow and LogicMonitor extend Edwin AI investigations in ServiceNow with new agent‑to‑agent capabilities.

🧩 How it works

  • Workflows are continuously analyzed and refined by AI agents, creating an ongoing improvement cycle.
  • The system leverages agentic AI, meaning AI entities act autonomously to identify and apply enhancements.
  • Agent‑to‑agent capabilities allow separate AI components (e.g., Edwin AI, Work4Flow, LogicMonitor) to cooperate on investigations and optimizations.

⚙️ Key details

  • Continuous, self‑optimizing workflow loop.
  • Agentic AI that can act without direct human commands.
  • Instant deployment of the Flow AI service desk.
  • Integration of multiple AI agents for deeper investigations (Edwin AI, Work4Flow, LogicMonitor).

🚀 Availability

  • Flow by ServiceNow can be deployed immediately after announcement.
  • AI Workflow Factory is positioned as a new service offering from ServiceNow.

💡 Why it matters

  • Enables enterprises to keep their processes up‑to‑date automatically.
  • Reduces the manual effort required to monitor and improve workflows.
  • Combines multiple AI agents to broaden investigative reach and accelerate problem resolution.

#ServiceNow #AIWorkflow #AgenticAI #Automation

Source: ServiceNow, Inc. (NOW) latest press releases and corporate news – Yahoo Finance

item.title: Foley Law Firm Advances Generative AI with Blueprint Methodology and Award-Winning FoleyChat
item.description:
Foley Law Firm Advances Generative AI with Blueprint Methodology and Award-Winning FoleyChat

Foley, a major law firm, has rolled out a structured AI Blueprint and its proprietary chatbot, FoleyChat, which won the Best Use of Artificial Intelligence Award at Legalweek 2026.

🔍 Overview

  • Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is no longer a novelty in legal services.
  • By early 2026, 74% of lawyers, tax advisors, and other professionals reported using AI several times a week.
  • In corporate law departments, generative AI use more than doubled in twelve months to 52%.

📊 Client Expectations

  • Nearly 80% of corporate clients say AI‑enabled quality is “very important or essential” when selecting advisors, while only 6% believe they receive it.
  • 32% of disappointed clients have reconsidered or plan to reconsider law‑firm relationships based on the use of AI, and among those clients, one‑third estimate that more than $1 million in annual work is at risk.

🛠️ Foley’s AI Approach

Pillar Description
Design Workflows are superior to lists of tools.
Authorization Insist on an owner for agentic work; an attorney must authorize, review, and be accountable for the AI output.
Proof Use of AI (e.g., eDiscovery) must be defensible; requires validation, sampling protocols, escalation procedures, and audit trails tracking attorney decisions.
Accountability A defensible workflow documents source materials, AI outputs, attorney revisions, and the authority supporting the final work product.

🤖 FoleyChat and Other Tools

Tool Use Case
FoleyChat Enables attorneys to build proprietary agents for recurring legal tasks; IP team uses it to stress‑test claim amendments and arguments against patent materials, prior art, and examiner data.
Relativity aiR Compresses discovery review from weeks or months to days.
Harvey & CoCounsel Identify and organize key authorities so attorney time focuses on strategy rather than only research.

🚀 Impact on Practice

  • Foley’s attorneys have integrated AI into pre‑existing workstreams, such as using AI throughout a deal’s lifecycle to surface diligence findings early and benchmark drafted language against filing databases.
  • Litigators employ AI‑assisted review to shift attorney effort from pure research to strategic advice.
  • The objective is faster, more consistent work that gives clients earlier decisions on a more complete record.
  • Through its Practice Innovation program, Foley leverages AI across diligence, legal research, and contract drafting by partnering legal‑technology teams with practice groups to deliver vetted AI solutions.
  • Foley’s AI Blueprint methodology starts with a legal task, maps where AI adds value, and specifies inputs, source documents, and quality‑control checkpoints before a workflow earns “validated” status.

#LegalTech #GenerativeAI #AIWorkflow

Source: Foley at the Forefront: From AI Adoption to Execution

item.title: Evidence‑Constrained Workflow for Research Commercialization Assessment Launched
item.description:
Evidence‑Constrained Workflow for Research Commercialization Assessment Launched

A new system that assesses the commercial potential of research papers using an evidence‑constrained workflow has been released.

🔍 Overview

  • Collect sources, analyse technical maturity, patents and market signals, then deliver a cited report with an auditable scorecard.
  • Built with Python, CrewAI, FastAPI and a build‑free JavaScript client.
  • Retrieval is deterministic; six LLM stages reason over validated evidence.
  • Supplementary Tool Calling is experimental and remains disconnected from production.

🛠️ How it works

  • Submit a research topic or attach a paper PDF; choose report language and scoring profile.
  • Follow progress, inspect citations and reliability warnings, export Markdown or PDF, and share a run link.
  • Recover an interrupted run as an immutable child using its longest validated checkpoint prefix and fresh credentials.
  • Access via operator‑issued access code or supported bring‑your‑own‑key (BYOK) credentials on a gated deployment.
  • Three evidence specialists run in parallel; Writer, Reviewer and Scorer follow in sequence.
  • Source‑native clients plus web search; URL/DOI checks, provenance tiers, deduplication and registered source IDs.
  • Pydantic contracts, guardrails, deterministic scoring and bounded Reviewer corrections.
  • Non‑blocking precision‑first claim/citation screens; unavailable checks are distinct from passes.
  • Subprocess isolation, content‑addressed checkpoints, immutable recovery children and write‑once terminal records.
  • Shared run/PDF admission, persistent daily operator‑funded quota and complete/lower‑bound/unavailable usage states.
  • Optional redacted OpenTelemetry/OpenInference traces to Phoenix or another OTLP collector.
  • FastAPI, vanilla HTML/CSS/ES modules, Docker and Railway; one application replica.
  • Use Python 3.11 or 3.12 for the CI‑tested environment and uv.

⚙️ Key details

Role Execution Mode
Evidence Specialist Parallel
Writer Sequential
Reviewer Sequential
Scorer Sequential

📊 Performance metrics

  • Frozen baseline: 10 topics × 3 live repetitions; End‑to‑end completion 30/30, TRL calibration 26/30, Weighted formula correctness 30/30, Complete report structure 30/30, Unsupported numeric lines 0 across 30 reports; seven of ten topics met their TRL range in all three runs.
  • Four‑node arm used 54.89 % fewer median tokens and 47.03 % lower median cost than the six‑node arm.
  • 30/30 offline fault‑injection children completed; one production child reused four committed nodes.
  • One normal Qwen completion passed 12/12 primary terminal checks, with a disclosed minor observer‑cadence deviation.
  • Production remains phase‑1 zero‑call shadow mode: gap signals may be recorded, but they do not add sources or paid searches.
  • Adaptive Role‑Gap v8 passed its AC development gates but failed three of six gates on AD unseen evaluation: routing 5/8, closure‑role value 2/7, and only +1 coverable case over the anchor.

🚀 Availability

  • Deployed on Docker and Railway with a single application replica.
  • Operates behind a gated deployment; users obtain access via an operator‑issued code or BYOK credentials.
  • Optional telemetry can be sent as redacted OpenTelemetry/OpenInference traces to Phoenix or another OTLP collector.

#AIWorkflow #ResearchAutomation #EvidenceBasedAI

Source: shuxiachai/academic-commercialization-agent

item.title: Using Claude and n8n to Query Ghost Content via API
item.description:
Using Claude and n8n to Query Ghost Content via API

I built a workflow that lets me query my Ghost‑hosted posts beyond the built‑in search.

🔍 Overview

  • Problem: I can’t query my published content hosted on Ghost beyond using the basic search capabilities.
  • Solution: By connecting the Ghost API endpoint with a Postgres‑hosted SaaS, an n8n sync workflow, a Claude Skill, and Claude Desktop, I can perform richer queries.

🧩 How it works

  • Ghost API endpoint – provides programmatic access to published posts.
  • Postgres‑hosted SaaS – stores the content for fast querying.
  • n8n sync workflow – automates data extraction and synchronization.
  • Claude Skill – interprets natural‑language queries.
  • Claude Desktop – runs the skill locally for quick responses.

⚙️ Key details

  • The combined setup enables query capabilities that go beyond Ghost’s native search.
  • The workflow was assembled in just a few hours, illustrating how quickly a problem can become a viable solution.
  • I am considering reproducing the same design to query content on Micro.blog.

🚀 Availability

  • The solution is a personal workflow built with publicly available tools; it is not a commercial product.

💡 Why it matters

  • Demonstrates a practical, low‑effort way to extend the functionality of existing SaaS platforms using AI and automation tools.

#Ghost #Claude #n8n #AIworkflow

Source: Photos
